name: Mossi kingdoms
summary: Kingdoms of the Mossi people on the Volta plateau, led by the Mogho Naba of Ouagadougou; they resisted the Mali and Songhai empires and Islam for centuries until the French conquered them in 1896.

knownFor.label: Mogho Naba
knownFor.note: The king of Ouagadougou, still a ceremonial figure.

location.value: Kingdoms in modern Burkina Faso along the upper Volta river.

terrain.value: A savanna plateau of rolling plains, with the Volta rivers.

climate.value: Hot, with a single rainy season from June to September.

disasters.value: Droughts and the famines that followed.

population.value: The page gives no population figure.

urbanisation.value: Mostly villages; a royal capital and market towns.

disease.value: Malaria and other tropical diseases; smallpox outbreaks.

migration.value: Founders came from the Dagbon area to the south (traditions).

economicBase.value: The page says foreign trade expanded across Africa in the 18th century, with links to the Fula kingdoms and the Mali Empire. Farming and trade in horses, salt and kola are not mentioned.

tradeRoutes.value: Routes between the forest and the Niger bend.

wealth.value: Moderate wealth, based on farming and tribute.

moneyAndTax.value: Tribute, market taxes and trade goods; cowrie shells in many markets.

inequality.value: Rulers and nobles above free farmers; enslaved people at the bottom.

governmentType.value: Five kingdoms: Ouagadougou (the largest), Tenkodogo, Fada N’gourma, Zondoma (later replaced by Yatenga) and Boussouma; the king of Ouagadougou, the Mogho Naaba, served as emperor of all the Mossi.

keyRulers.value: The Mogho Naaba, king of Ouagadougou, was emperor of all the Mossi; Naba Baongo II reigns today.

succession.value: The Mogho Naba was chosen from the royal lineage by a council of electors.

institutions.value: Court officials, ministers and earth priests who guarded the land.

armyAndTech.value: Cavalry with spears and bows, and strong horses.

majorWars.value: In the 15th century the Mossi took Timbuktu and sacked Walata (no year given); the French took over in 1896 and created Upper Volta.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Mossi Kingdoms (checked 13 Nov 2026); Britannica: Mossi states (checked 15 Nov 2026) (fast light cavalry raided the Mali empire and competed with Songhai for the Middle Niger; the Timbuktu raid is not mentioned)

territoryChange.value: The kingdoms changed little between 1500 and 1890.

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals of Songhai, and wary of Muslim neighbours.

scienceEducation.value: Oral learning; Qur’anic schools where Islam spread.

openness.value: Open to trade but resistant to outside rule and conversion.

communicationTransport.value: Footpaths and caravan routes carried goods and messages.

religion.value: The Mossi largely kept their traditional religious and ritual practices; Islam is also listed in the infobox.

languageWriting.value: Mooré, an oral language with no writing until the colonial era.

artsArchitecture.value: Masks and elaborate royal ceremonies, notably at the court in Ouagadougou.

sharedIdentity.value: Loyalty to the Mogho Naba and the shared ancestral lineage.

dailyLife.value: Families farmed millet and sorghum in villages, with royal ceremonies marking the year.

ideasReligions.value: Traditional beliefs, with the king as a sacred figure; Islam was resisted for centuries.

riseSignals.value: Oral history of the princess Yennenga and her son Ouedraogo, who built Tenkodogo, is dated anywhere from the 11th to the 15th century; Oubri is called founder of the Ouagadougou dynasty (c. 1050–1090 in the article).
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Mossi Kingdoms (checked 13 Nov 2026); Britannica: Mossi states (checked 15 Nov 2026) (Britannica says the ancestors came from the east, perhaps in the 13th century, but the origins of the kingdoms are unclear, which supports keeping this disputed)

peakPeriod.value: The page names no peak; its map shows the area held c. 1530. Ouagadougou was the largest kingdom. The French took over in 1896.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Mossi Kingdoms (checked 13 Nov 2026); Britannica: Mossi states (checked 15 Nov 2026) (Britannica gives no peak; it says the Mossi were trade go-betweens for the forest states and the Niger cities from about 1400)

outcome.value: The French entered in 1896, conquered the Mossi Kingdom and made it part of Upper Volta; the last king of Ouagadougou died in 1904.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Mossi Kingdoms (checked 13 Nov 2026); Britannica: Mossi states (checked 15 Nov 2026) (Britannica gives the span as about 1500–1895 and says the Mossi kept their independence until the French invasions of the late 19th century; it gives no 1896 date)

overallCertainty.value: Known from oral traditions, travellers and colonial records; many dates are approximate.
